key_insight: Action Images unifies action representation and video modeling by learning pixel-grounded, multiview video generation end-to-end, enabling policies that directly leverage pretrained video backbones and generalize across viewpoints.
problem_solved: Existing world action models separate action modules or use non-pixel-grounded action codes, which prevents full use of pretrained video models and limits transferability across viewpoints and environments.
method: Introduce pixel-grounded action representations that are injected into a video backbone to generate future frames from multiple viewpoints.
Train the system end-to-end on multiview video prediction, using generated multi-view futures as supervision for policy learning instead of detached action modules.
Leverage pretrained video backbones to bootstrap visual dynamics and enforce viewpoint-invariant action grounding, improving generalization across scenes and camera angles.
impact: Provides a simpler, more transferable pipeline for robot policy learning that better exploits pretrained video models; improves robustness to viewpoint changes and reduces hand-designed action abstractions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image(s) -> pixel-grounded action tokens -> pretrained video backbone -> multiview future frames -> policy output
Before vs After comparison: separated action-module pipeline vs unified Action Images approach (showing reduced components and direct pixel grounding)
Overlay heatmaps: pixel-grounded action maps on example frames demonstrating where actions are anchored in the image
Performance chart: generalization across viewpoints/environments (e.g., drops in error or gains in success rate) and sample-efficiency bar plot
paper_title: Action Images: End-to-End Policy Learning via Multiview Video Generation
paper_authors: Haoyu Zhen, Zixian Gao, Qiao Sun, Yilin Zhao, Yuncong Yang
